doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Saxophone influences and Mingus calling him best jazz flutist
summary: Hubert Laws and Joe Farrell are listened to, but Parker, Getz and Konitz influenced him most; Mingus and Mariano praised him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Who were the other jazz players that you’ve listened to and enjoyed or not enjoyed?

I listen to a lot of the people like Hubert Laws and Joe Farrell. In fact most of my influence has been more like saxophone players you see. So that’s why I associate the bebop thing and the style plus my own whatever I do with those influences. So it seems like I listen to more saxophone players than flutists. I like a lot of these people. I was just more influenced by Charlie Parker and Stan Getz and Lee Konitz, that type of thing.
You had some pretty nice compliments from — Charles Mingus called you the world’s greatest jazz flute player.
Yeah, well don’t forget he put out that album—
Yeah, well that helps, doesn’t it.

But he did like that. But he came into a club I was in in New York and as he came in he goes, “There’s Sam Most, the world’s greatest jazz flute player” whether he meant it or not. But it was nice. And also another one that called me his favorite bebop flutist was Charlie Mariano. I haven’t seen him for a long time. And okay.
